issues.issue: Three raw record ids (d591db2c-0a82-482e-a8c8-5f93768b9a24, 69e48d8e849ab9426f17022d, composer-5gohk1e06) print as unlabelled body text between the breadcrumb and the Tracks heading.
Three header controls compete at equal weight: Create (purple filled), Ask Co-Creator (outlined), and Export all sitting inside a white focus ring that makes the secondary action look live.

Every audio-library item truncates its metadata mid-word (00:15 transportation • mo..., 00:14 transportation + mo...) and the collection tile reads Educati..., cutting the length and mood that decide the pick.

The whole window behind the open row menu is washed to one pale gray, so the selected Ram Create Clips row, the Name/Duration/Created headers and the sidebar labels all sit within a couple of steps of each other in value.
No video frame appears anywhere on the editor screen: the transcript document and two right-hand columns fill the width, so the clip itself is never visible while trimming.

Two parallel navigation systems stack on the right, the AI Tools list with its own search box and a second icon rail (Project, Properties, Elements, Captions, Stock, Underlord), and neither marks which panel is showing.
In the top row (ENG-139) the label pills clip into each other and truncate to 1.5, Squa..., Migra..., which pushes the issue title to Identify Missing Data ... and makes the row unreadable.
Seven tabs (Engineering, All issues, Active, Backlog, Recent Urgent Bugs, 5 more...) plus Filter and Display stack at one weight above the list, so nothing is the focal point.
The issue body has no visible edit affordance: no toolbar, no edit control near the title or the description, so there is nothing on the screen that says what to do next.
Add more credits is the only filled, highest-contrast button on the screen while the clip grid carries no primary action of its own, so the paid control outranks reviewing the clips.
The Auto headline callout paragraph runs the full content width at over 100 characters per line, pushing the clip row well below the middle of the screen.
The left navigation rail is icon-only at any size (dot, four squares, list, folder, calendar, chart, link), with no label to identify any of the sections.
Each of the seven More tools tiles carries an AI badge overlapping the tile's top-right icon corner, so the badge collides with the glyph it is meant to qualify.
The right-hand Auto removal promo card, complete with three carousel dots, sits at the same visual weight as the Create project hero it sits beside.
The media toolbar labels (Media, Audio, Text, Stickers, Effects, Transitions, Filters) are the smallest type on the screen at roughly 10px, below the Details panel's labels.
Keep, Maybe and Skip render as three identical text links under every clip with no selected state on any row, including the open clip 01, so a decision already made cannot be read back.
Why this clip is a collapsed text row wedged between the In/Out/Length fields and the download row, so the reason for the 35.7 score is the quietest thing in the properties panel.
The disabled AI connection / Coming soon chip in the header uses the same gray as the muted metadata text, so it reads as an available control rather than a disabled one.

notes: Only P3 has a designed error screen, so every other product is scored on its two states with no failure or empty state to judge. P5's screens are an issue tracker rather than a video tool, so its cliplist state shows no clips to review.
